title: Invariant subspace problem relative to a von Neumann algebra
statement: Let $H$ be an infinite-dimensional separable Hilbert space. Is there, for arbitrary $T\in B(H)\setminus \mathbb{C}I$, a projection $p$ belonging to the von Neumann algebra generated by $T$ such that $p\notin\{0,1\}$ and $Tp=pTp$?
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/45](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12593), page 67. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

solutions.summary: Claimed by OpenAI. For every prescribed irrational angle, claims a continuous nonnegative circle weight with exactly one zero and logarithmic integral minus infinity whose weighted rotation has no nontrivial invariant projection in the associated hyperfinite II_1 factor. Arbitrary Hilbert-subspace projections outside that factor are not excluded.
solutions.body:
Claimed by OpenAI. For every prescribed irrational angle, claims a continuous nonnegative circle weight with exactly one zero and logarithmic integral minus infinity whose weighted rotation has no nontrivial invariant projection in the associated hyperfinite II_1 factor. Arbitrary Hilbert-subspace projections outside that factor are not excluded.

Scope relative to this problem: The source excludes nontrivial invariant projections in the associated hyperfinite II1 factor for its weighted-rotation operator, for every prescribed irrational angle. The von Neumann algebra generated by that operator lies inside the factor, so its projection assertion addresses the target factor-relative question. Arbitrary invariant Hilbert-subspace projections outside the factor are not excluded; this is not an ordinary invariant-subspace counterexample.
